mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real GDP signals a strong demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of periods following a 3-month GDP increase, or GDP growth and SPX returns show a negative correlation over a 5-year rolling window (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals weakening labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% over two months signals a supply-side contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate output and earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts by more than 5% over two months signals a strengthening demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate increased economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and the CPI is increasing by more than 0.3% per month, the combination signals an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced purchasing power and corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.2% within a month, the combination signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate increased consumer spending and corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decrease in retail and food services sales signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of periods following a 3-month RSAFS decrease, or RSAFS decreases and SPX returns show a positive correlation over a 5-year rolling window (p < 0.05).
